content.comment_body: Hello experts, I need to configure a setup with 17 digital inputs, 5 digital outputs, 2 analog inputs, and 2 analog outputs. Please recommend an economical and suitable selection of [product_name] modules to meet these requirements. My initial selection is: 1) [product_name] (8DI/4DO), 2) [product_name] (4DI/4DO), 3) [product_name] (2AI), 4) [product_name] (2AO). Your suggestions for cost-effective combinations are appreciated. Regards, [user_name]
Hello, I have a question: Why did you choose the 230 type? Is it to avoid using a separate power supply? Regards,

Dear [user_name], it's not about saving power supply, but rather it's based on my client's requirement; they need to operate two drive units (redundancy) along with [product_name] and DCS, all on 230 V AC control supply. Please respond to my previous question. Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], I suggest this full set: [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] (plus power supply for the analog modules). You'll need two [product_name] modules for your setup; the larger module is usually more cost-effective than two smaller ones. All analog modules can be connected after the digital ones. If possible to reduce one input, you may not need the second [product_name].
Thanks [user_name], How expandable is this setup? How many modules are supported in total? Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], With [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] + [product_name] (plus power supply for analog modules), you'll get: 20 digital inputs (230V AC), 16 digital outputs (relay), 2 analog inputs, and 2 analog outputs. You can also add another [product_name] and up to three more analog modules. The digital modules are available for 230V and also 12/24V, depending on station requirements. There is a brochure for series 6 and 7 available at [url]. More details can be found on the official site: [url].
Thank you, [user_name], for your help. One more question: Is it possible to communicate [product_name] over PROFIBUS? Regards, [user_name]

Hi [user_name], Direct communication over PROFIBUS is not possible with this [product_name]. It can be connected using KNX, AS-i, or [product_name] communication (for 7 series). For example, with [product_name] [article_no] only. More details at [url].

analysis.insight_summary: Participants are evaluating different combinations of [product_name] modules to achieve specific input/output capacities for a control system operating at 230 V AC. The conversation aims to find the most cost-effective and expandable selection, while clarifying module compatibility, extension limits, and the potential for communication integration. Users seek clear guidance on expansion limits and communication protocol options, but encounter uncertainty regarding module selection and communication capabilities.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect expert advice on a cost-efficient and expandable configuration of [product_name] modules that meets their exact I/O specifications and operates with a 230 V AC supply. They also want clear guidance on networking options such as integration with communication protocols like PROFIBUS.
